historical_anchors.JCS_12_March: JCS directive called for Saipan/Tinian/Guam occupation by 15 June and neutralization/bypass of Truk.
historical_anchors.Spruance_12_May: Fifth Fleet FORAGER operation plan issued for capture/development of the Marianas and B-29/central-Pacific strategic control.

branch_reassessment.Hollandia_absent: Removes one historical carrier-support commitment but does not remove FORAGER logistics, political momentum, or JCS authorization.
branch_reassessment.China_worse: Japanese success in China makes secure Marianas B-29 basing at least as attractive, arguably more attractive, than relying on China-based heavy-bomber logistics.
branch_reassessment.US_carrier_state: Fast-carrier force is strong and still expanding; no branch attrition shock large enough to force strategic pause.
branch_reassessment.Japanese_defense: Marianas defenses are stronger than historical baseline, increasing preparatory-strike/cover requirements but not crossing a cancellation threshold.
branch_reassessment.political_institutional_inertia: The operation is already a joint approved campaign with amphibious shipping, rehearsals and Army/Marine formations committed. Reversal in late May would require a major new strategic shock. None exists.

decision: FORAGER_GO; retain 15 June Saipan D-Day as planning center
acceleration: NO. Do not pull D-Day materially earlier merely because Hollandia is absent; amphibious rehearsals, loading, intelligence, naval gunfire coordination and staging are hard schedule constraints.
stop_gate: FAILED; there is no military/political basis for a late-May strategic pause.
future_guard: Force composition must be rebuilt from branch carrier/damage state before D-Day; historical deck count cannot be copied blindly.
